title: Hats handed back at random
hook: Does a bigger crowd make it less likely that anyone gets their own hat?

knows: how to find the chance of at least one event
doesNotKnow: that the chance of at least one match barely depends on the number of people

misconception: With more people it is less likely that anyone gets their own hat back.
objective: The learner can explain that more people means more chances for a match but a smaller chance each, so the chance of at least one match stays near 63% from 10 people to 1,000.
keyState: Runs at 3, 10, 100 and 1,000 people, each showing a matched share near 66.7%, 63.2%, 63.2%, 63.2%.

claims.text: Model: the hats come back in a uniformly random order, and each shuffle gives every hat to one person; each run is 1,000 shuffles. Stated on the stage.
claims.source: Hat-check (derangement) problem; stage text 'Toy: each shuffle hands every hat to a random person.' | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Demo.tsx run(): Fisher-Yates uniform shuffle, 1,000 per run; stage label states it.

claims.text: The chance that at least one of n people gets their own hat is 1 - (1 - 1 + 1/2! - 1/3! ...): 66.7% for 3 people, 63.2% for 10, 63.2% for 100 and 63.2% for 1,000.
As the crowd grows the chance approaches 1 - 1/e, about 63.2%: more people give more chances for a match, but each is a smaller chance (1 in n), and the two cancel.
claims.source: limit of the series is 1 - 1/e = 0.632121 (node). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): sum (-1)^k/k! -> 1/e; 1 - 1/e = 0.6321206.

claims.text: The learner's first runs of 1,000 shuffles at 3 / 10 / 100 / 1,000 people (shown in the reveal) were 66.9% / 63.5% / 62.0% / 62.1%; runs of 1,000 shuffles scatter by about a point or two.
claims.source: mulberry32(size * 7919 + batch), batch 0, first seeds tried, untuned (node, same run() as Demo.tsx). Batch 1: 67.8 / 61.6 / 63.5 / 62.9. Binomial noise of 1,000 trials at 63%: standard deviation 1.5 points. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): node, own copy of run(): batch 0 = 66.9 / 63.5 / 62.0 / 62.1, batch 1 = 67.8 / 61.6 / 63.5 / 62.9; sd sqrt(.632 x .368 / 1000) = 1.5 points.

recall.question: 100 people check hats and get them back in random order. Compared with 10 people, the chance that at least one gets their own hat is:
recall.why: More people means more chances for a match, but each chance shrinks to 1 in n. They cancel, so the chance stays near 1 - 1/e, about 63%.
